A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Latte/Latte-Macchiato research, despite the changed title and substantial reorganization. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original language-modelling, LRA, Gemma adaptation, latent-state and runtime experiments, including additional analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains original Latte experiments and additionally reports MQAR and downstream language-benchmark outcomes.

M1.justification: The core Latte factorization, causal recurrence, Macchiato mixture and convolution/RGLRU extensions remain equivalent; the directed terminology does not establish a new algorithm. v5 withdraws the separately proposed VAPOR value-rotation extension from v3 Appendix B.3. Whether VAPOR was removed from implementations underlying retained results is not established.

E1.justification: v5 adds MQAR associative recall and eight downstream language benchmarks, including MMLU, HellaSwag and Lambada. Existing language-modelling, LRA and BookCorpus extrapolation coverage remains, but the explicit sequence-truncation scenario disappears. Table 4 newly names Tiny-Stories as pretraining data, while Section 5.4 still specifies SlimPajama only, leaving that training-coverage change unresolved.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds GLA, Lightning Attention-2 and GatedDeltaNet. The full-model runtime comparison adds Flash Attention in v5 Figure 8. Conversely, Table 3 removes BigBird from the LRA comparison; Linear Transformer becoming Linear Att. and RGLRU becoming R are renamings.

E3.justification: The language-model settings table changes substantially: v3 Table 5 versus v5 Table 6 specifies 12 versus 8 layers, 128 versus 256 latent states, 1024 versus 512 sequence length, and 100K versus 200K iterations. BookCorpus extrapolation changes the standard-attention baseline from ROPE to YaRN. MQAR introduces 100K training and 10K test examples with state-size and sequence-length sweeps. These reported changes do not establish reruns of retained results.

E4.justification: v5 removes v3 Figure 5's latent-capacity and sequence-truncation analyses, Appendix C's isolated-layer runtime/memory and state-count sensitivity analyses, and Figure 11's comprehensive latent-state heatmaps. Component ablations and three representative heatmaps remain. MQAR adds recall sensitivity evidence, while BookCorpus extrapolation is retained in Appendix B with a revised baseline setting.

E5.justification: v3 Figure 4 explicitly reports 100 timing runs; corresponding v5 Figure 8 retains standard-deviation reporting but omits the run count. The 100-repeat disclosures accompanying removed appendix efficiency plots also disappear. This is reduced statistical documentation, not evidence that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: Existing Table 1 results, retained LRA rows and Gemma perplexities remain numerically identical. v5 adds MQAR, Flash Attention and downstream results, plus Table 2 perplexities of 19.10 for GLA, 23.67 for Lightning Attention-2 and 21.41 for GatedDeltaNet. New Table 5 reports MMLU accuracy of 46.8 for Gemma-Macchiato versus 53.0 for Gemma. Extrapolation curves are replaced under revised settings, and several diagnostic and inference results disappear.

T1.justification: v5 Section 3 adds a mathematical derivation of positive-feature linear attention as an undirected latent graphical model and develops its comparison with the directed factorization. The underlying Latte equations remain equivalent. v3's explicit complexity derivation, VAPOR derivation and detailed mathematical treatment of Luna are removed; the stable scan implementation remains.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction shift from presenting a latent attention mechanism to claiming a unifying graphical-model account of linear attention. New central claims identify absent directionality in conventional linear attention and motivate Latte through asymmetric dependencies and properly normalized hybrid attention. The earlier context-extension and competitive-performance claims remain elsewhere in v5.

C2.justification: v5 adds directionality and normalization as mechanism explanations, excludes sparse attention and unnormalized recurrent mixers from the framework, and discusses downstream accuracy losses and JAX/CUDA comparison limitations. It also describes Latte as approximating full attention, whereas v3 Section 2.1 explicitly distinguishes its parameterization from approximation. Earlier capacity and short-sequence speed tradeoff discussions disappear.

D1.justification: v5 replaces the experiment-specific, three-column language-model hyperparameter table with a different generic table, losing dedicated analysis and extrapolation settings. Numerical-stability explanations and efficiency reproduction details are removed. Conversely, it replaces the dummy repository URL with a concrete GitHub address and specifies four A100 GPUs for all experiments. The causal scan listing is retained rather than newly supplied.

R1.justification: The paper is repositioned around directed versus undirected probabilistic models and normalized hybrid attention. v5 adds references concerning associative recall, GLA, YaRN, GatedDeltaNet and language-model linearization. The detailed Luna comparison is shortened, and Shen et al.'s bidirectional mechanism changes from being described as equivalent to being described as similar in form.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, with an explicit contribution list and new Background and graphical-model sections. Experiments are reorganized, related work moves after them, and a limitations section is added. The appendices are substantially restructured and model names shortened, beyond ordinary copyediting.

P2.justification: v5 adopts a different journal layout and stacks formerly side-by-side Tables 1 and 2. It adds graphical-model diagrams, an MQAR plot and a downstream-results table; revises runtime and extrapolation displays; and removes the architecture diagram and several diagnostic displays. The hyperparameter table structure and code-listing presentation also change.

improvement.justification: v5 broadens empirical scrutiny through MQAR, newer comparators, Flash Attention and downstream benchmarks, with Table 5 usefully exposing capability losses. However, it removes substantial sensitivity and efficiency evidence and replaces experiment-specific settings with an unreconciled generic table despite retaining the main numerical results. These benefits and losses, particularly the uncertain mapping between reported settings and results, prevent a reliable net assessment of overall quality.
